rounds.text: Kross Ltd demonstrates strong historical growth, highlighted by a compounded profit growth rate of 64% over five years [E17] and a 30% compounded sales growth over the same period [E14]. This fundamental outperformance is supported by robust return metrics, including a ROCE of 15.29% compared to a sector benchmark of 12.77% [E10] and an ROA of 9.06% versus a sector benchmark of 6.37% [E8]. Furthermore, the intrinsic value derived from a discounted cash flow model sits at Rs 366 per share, offering a 25.7% margin of safety against the market price of Rs 272 [E38, E39]. The company is also conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.11x [E31], and it is actively expanding its future capacity, evidenced by Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) surging by 1500.0% to Rs 16 Cr in March 2026 [E33]. Momentum is solidly backing these fundamentals, with the stock holding a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E44] and trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43]. Conceded: free cash flow stands at a negative Rs -72 Cr in March 2026 alongside a low cash conversion ratio of 0.51x [E28, E30].

The stock trades at an elevated P/E of 30.4 [E1] and sits near its 52-week peak [E41, E42], while momentum metrics explicitly flag that price growth has outpaced profit growth by 36%, meaning market expectations are running far ahead of actual delivery [E50]. Beneath the headline earnings, cash generation is deeply concerning: cash conversion sits at a weak 0.51x with profits far ahead of cash due to mounting receivables and accruals [E28], culminating in a severe negative free cash flow of Rs -72 Cr in Mar 2026 [E30]. This cash burn is accompanied by rising borrowings, which jumped from Rs 34 Cr to Rs 54 Cr [E32], alongside a steep deterioration in working capital efficiency as working capital days ballooned from 86.9 to 124 days [E54]. Furthermore, institutional exodus is clear as foreign and domestic institutions have cut their holdings by 2.56 and 3.44 percentage points respectively since Sep 2024 [E35, E36], and the company offers a 0.00% dividend yield despite reporting profits [E4, E53]. Conceded: the rules-based screen scores an 83 out of 100 on the back of strong historical profit growth and solid sales figures [E55, E56, E57, E58, E59].

Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated P/E of 30.4 [E1] near its 52-week peak [E41, E42], and price growth has recently outpaced profit growth [E50]. However, the valuation is fundamentally supported by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 366 per share, which provides a tangible 25.7% margin of safety [E38, E39]. Conceded: cash conversion is 0.51x with a negative free cash flow of Rs -72 Cr [E28, E30] and borrowings rose to Rs 54 Cr [E32], but this capital expenditure build-up is directly explained by a massive 1500% surge in capital-work-in-progress to Rs 16 Cr, representing aggressive growth spend underway rather than operational decay [E33]. Conceded: institutional holdings have declined [E35, E36], but total promoter stake increased to 68.57% and overall institutional money flow actually registers as positive with a holding change of +0.91 percentage points [E34, E37]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4, E53], but the underlying business compensates shareholders through exceptional multi-year wealth creation, highlighted by a 5-year compounded profit growth of 64% [E17] and a rules-based screen score of 83 out of 100 [E55].

The Bull’s reliance on a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 366 [E38, E39] is undermined by the reality that earnings growth is already decelerating [E60], with trailing twelve-month profit growth falling to 13% [E19], which is significantly lower than the 18% growth the DCF base case assumes [E40]. While the Bull attributes negative free cash flow of Rs -72 Cr [E30] to growth-oriented capital-work-in-progress [E33], this ignores deteriorating operational efficiency as working capital days have ballooned from 86.9 to 124 days [E54] and cash conversion remains a weak 0.51x [E28]. Conceded: promoter holdings increased slightly [E34] and money flow is positive [E37], yet the substantial retreat of foreign institutions by 2.56 percentage points [E35] and domestic institutions by 3.44 percentage points [E36] suggests professional investors are exiting as price growth outpaces profit growth by 36% [E50]. Conceded: historical 5-year profit growth was 64% [E17, E52], but the Bull ignores the clear multi-year erosion in returns, with median return on equity dropping from a 5-year average of 19% [E21] to just 12% last year [E23], all while the company fails to pay dividends [E53]. Finally, the Bull's valuation defense ignores that the current P/E of 30.23x and EV/EBITDA of 18.44x are significantly higher than sector benchmarks of 24.41x and 11.81x [E6, E11], a premium that is difficult to justify given that operating margins have remained stagnant at 13% over the last three years [E24] and the margin trend is inconsistent [E26, E27].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth of 13% [E19] sits below the DCF base assumption [E40], and institutional holdings have indeed receded [E35, E36]. However, the reverse DCF proves that the current market price only requires a modest 13.9% earnings growth, meaning expectations are not overly inflated [E40]. The negative free cash flow [E30] and ballooning working capital [E54] are the natural consequence of a massive 1500% surge in capital-work-in-progress, which represents aggressive, future-focused capacity expansion rather than structural decay [E33]. While the bear highlights premium valuation multiples [E6, E11], those higher ratios are entirely justified by a superior return on capital employed of 15.29% against the sector benchmark of 12.77% [E10], alongside a stellar 5-year compounded profit growth of 64% [E17]. Finally, the claim of eroded returns ignores that median return on equity over 3 years remains a healthy 17% [E22], while the rules-based screen affirms a strong BUY score of 83 out of 100 [E55].

Conceded: [E10] and [E17]. The bull's reliance on the reverse DCF demanding only a 13.9% growth rate [E40] ignores that actual earnings growth is actively decelerating [E60], with TTM profit growth slipping to 13% [E19] and quarterly margins remaining inconsistent [E27]. The claim that negative free cash flow of -72 Cr [E30] and ballooning working capital days expanding from 86.9 to 124 days [E54] are benign growth symptoms is contradicted by a poor cash conversion ratio of 0.51x, which signals that reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash collection and points to underlying receivables or accrual risks [E28]. Furthermore, smart money is actively fleeing the narrative as foreign and domestic institutional holdings have dropped significantly over the past two years [E35, E36], directly conflicting with the idea of broad-based conviction behind these expansion efforts. While the bull points to a solid 3-year median ROE [E22], current trailing ROE has compressed down to 12.0% [E13], matching the sector benchmark [E9] and showing that historical strength is fading while debt climbs to 54 Cr [E32]. Finally, chasing a stock sitting 95% up its 52-year range [E41] with a price-led divergence where price growth exceeds profit growth by 36% [E50] exposes investors to severe volatility of 55.4% [E47] and a proven peak-to-trough drawdown risk of -40.5% [E46].
